pr_body:
When ES sits behind a proxy/NAT wrt HTTP clients, the ES node admin has the option to include the IP/DNS in the ES settings in order for the node to advertise the addresses that it can be reached at, in the node info APIs (the publish addresses are not used for binding).

This PR makes the HTTPs certificates that Security auto-configuration generates to include the publish addresses in the certificate's SAN. This way, other nodes can enroll across NATed envs.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/81313
pr_title: Auto-generated HTTPs cert SAN includes publish addresses

review_comment: Not all hostnames, can be DNS names. Should we devise a regexp for DNS names? I don't think there's a problem if we include invalid DNS names in the SAN.

What are some examples you are thinking of ? If "cannot be DNS names" means simply that this will not be resolved by a DNS server that the host machine is configured to use then we can't know on configuration time right ?

For instance I think that `somestring` is a valid dnsName value for a SAN

https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5280.html#section-4.2.1.6 says :

> When the subjectAltName extension contains a domain name system
   label, the domain name MUST be stored in the dNSName (an IA5String).
   The name MUST be in the "preferred name syntax", as specified by
   Section 3.5 of [RFC1034] and as modified by Section 2.1 of
   [RFC1123].
   
 and https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc1034#section-3.5 sees to allow a domain that includes a simple `<label>`
 
 I think we don't need to do anything additional here

Thanks for digging those up Ioannis!

Apologies for being vague, I was thinking that maybe `hostname` and `domain name` have different grammars, such that a `hostname` cannot be used in place of a `domain name`.
However, the internets ([networking - Valid characters of a hostname? - Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3523028/valid-characters-of-a-hostname) and [RFC 952: DoD Internet host table specification](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc952) ) says that the `hostname` IS a `domain name`.
good call. Not only these are not used for validation but will probably ( apart from the localhost related ones ) be _wrong_ for the other nodes that will get this certificate :+1:
